07/15.05.2024 Heard Mr. Pratiush Lala, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Mr. Rajneesh Vardhan, learned A.P.P assisted by Mr. Pratik Singh, learned counsel appearing for the informant.
This interlocutory application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail during the pendency of this appeal.
The appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 376(3) and 366 IPC and Section 6 read with Section 5(1) of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced accordingly.
It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant was implicated on account of enticing away the informant, who was a minor at the time of the incident.

It has been submitted that during the trial, the appellant was on bail and after the informant had attained majority marriage has also been solemnized by the petitioner with the informant on 17.07.2022.
Some photographs in support of such marriage have also been brought on record through this interlocutory application.

Learned counsel appearing for the informant has accepted the submissions advanced by Mr.
Pratiush Lala, learned counsel for the appellant.

In view of the fact that the appellant has solemnized marriage with the informant after she has attained majority and this fact having been accepted by the learned counsel for the informant, the Banti Kumar Das vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34059044/
1 appellant during the pendency of this appeal is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Special Judge-POCSO Act, Dhanbad.
